text.p: Botswana has set up a Bureau of Standards amid a growing need for quality control as the economy diversifies from its reliance on diamonds into manufacturing, Commerce and Industry Minister George Kgoroba said on Monday.
Its launch was part of the government's revised policy on incomes, employment, prices and profits, which calls for a shift from price control to consumer protection, Kgoroba said.

"There was before no independent institution to verify the quality of any product produced in Botswana. Imported products either met the standards of their country of origin, or none at all," Kgoroba said.
The bureau has been funded under a technical cooperation agreement between Botswana and Germany.

Gilbert Motsemme, deputy permanent secretary responsible for industry, said the bureau would initially concentrate on the health and safety aspects of food production, the manufacture of electrical goods and engineering produts.
Motsemme said legislation to protect intellectual property in Botswana could be expected soon.
